candidates.label: earlyPrepaymentPenalty
candidates.comment: An early prepayment penalty relation between a repayment specification and a monetary amount, representing the fee for paying off a loan ahead of schedule. Also called "prepayment fee", "early payoff penalty", "exit fee". Examples: "Mortgage repayment earlyPrepaymentPenalty '$500'", "Loan agreement earlyPrepaymentPenalty '2% of remaining balance'", "Car loan earlyPrepaymentPenalty '$100'".

candidates.label: netWorth
candidates.comment: The total financial value of a person, calculated as assets minus liabilities. Also called personal wealth, financial worth, total assets. Examples: "Person A netWorth '$1,000,000'", "Person B netWorth '$500,000'", "Person C netWorth '$10,000'".

candidates.label: incomeLimit
candidates.comment: A financial constraint relation indicating the maximum income for which a financial incentive is applicable. Also called income cap, income threshold, maximum income, income eligibility. Examples: A tax credit has an incomeLimit of $100,000. A scholarship has an incomeLimit of '150% of poverty line'. A housing subsidy has an incomeLimit of $75,000.

candidates.label: taxID
candidates.comment: An identification of the tax or fiscal ID for an organization or person. Also called "fiscal ID", "tax identification number", "TIN", "VAT number". Examples: "The organization has taxID 12-3456789", "The person's taxID is their Social Security Number", "This company's taxID is its CIF."

candidates.label: financialAidEligible
candidates.comment: A financial aid eligibility relation between a course or educational program and the types of financial aid students can use to cover its costs. Also called: aid programs, funding options, scholarship eligibility. Examples: "Computer Science Course" financial aid eligible "Federal Pell Grant", "MBA Program" financial aid eligible "Student Loans", "Vocational Training" financial aid eligible "GI Bill".

candidates.label: legislationResponsible
candidates.comment: A responsibility relation between a piece of legislation and the individual or organization accountable for its elaboration or inquiries. Also called: responsible for, overseen by, managed by. Examples: "Health Act legislationResponsible Ministry of Health", "Environmental Law legislationResponsible EPA", "Tax Reform legislationResponsible Treasury Department". Distinct from legislationPassedBy, which refers to the original enacting authority.

candidates.label: referee

Examples: "A football match has a referee 'Pierluigi Collina'.", "A tennis match has a referee 'Eva Asderaki-Moore'.", "A basketball game has a referee 'Joey Crawford'."

candidates.label: contraindication

candidates.label: price

A product has a price of '100'. The service has a price of '50.00'. Distinct from priceCurrency, which specifies the currency of the price.

candidates.label: yearlyRevenue

Also called annual revenue, annual income, gross annual earnings. Examples: TargetAudience yearlyRevenue "$1M - $5M", BusinessAudience yearlyRevenue "over $10M", StartupAudience yearlyRevenue "under $500K".

candidates.label: resultReview

candidates.label: reviews

candidates.label: reviewAspect

candidates.label: associatedReview

candidates.label: reviewRating

candidates.label: itemReviewed
candidates.comment: A review subject relation between an aggregate rating or review and the entity that is being evaluated or rated. candidates.label: reviewCount

relations.definition: To have possession or control of something

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: owner
candidates.comment: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder. Examples: "Car owner 'John Doe'", "Company owner 'Acme Corp'", "House owner 'Smith Family Trust'". Distinct from creator, who made the thing.

candidates.label: copyrightHolder
candidates.comment: A legal ownership relation between a creative work and the person or organization holding its copyright. Also called: copyright owner, rights holder, legally owned by. Examples: "The Mona Lisa" copyright holder "The Louvre Museum", "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" copyright holder "J.K. Rowling", "Microsoft Windows" copyright holder "Microsoft Corporation".

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: ownedFrom
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was obtained. Also called acquisition date, purchase date, date acquired. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2020-01-15'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2018-06-01T10:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2023-03-10'". Distinct from ownedThrough, which is the date ownership ended.

candidates.label: landlord

candidates.label: ownedThrough

candidates.label: numberOfPreviousOwners

Distinct from colleague, which indicates a professional relationship, or parent, which indicates a familial relationship.

chosen_property.label: threatened
chosen_property.definition: To communicate a threat or warning to someone or something
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation phrase and instances.

candidates.label: accessibilityHazard
candidates.comment: An accessibility hazard relation between a creative work and a characteristic that poses a physiological danger to some users. Also called accessibility risk, dangerous feature, user hazard. Examples: "A video's accessibility hazard is 'flashingLights'.", "A game's accessibility hazard is 'motionSimulation'."

candidates.label: risks
candidates.comment: The specific physiological dangers or adverse effects associated with a particular diet plan. Also called diet hazards, health risks of diet, diet side effects. Examples: `Keto Diet` risks `"Nutrient deficiencies"`, `Fad Diet` risks `"Metabolic imbalance"`, `Vegan Diet` risks `"Vitamin B12 deficiency if not supplemented"`.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: warning
candidates.comment: A warning relation between a drug and any FDA or other safety advisories. Also called drug warning, safety advisory, health alert. Examples: "Drug warning 'May cause drowsiness.'", "Drug warning 'https://fda.gov/drug-warnings/xyz'", "Medication warning 'Do not exceed recommended dose.'".

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: safetyConsideration
candidates.comment: Any potential safety concerns, interactions, or adverse reactions associated with a dietary supplement. Also called supplement warnings, safety warnings, adverse effects. Examples: `St. John's Wort` safetyConsideration `"May interact with antidepressants"`, `Creatine Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Not recommended for individuals with kidney issues"`, `Vitamin D Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Avoid excessive dosage"`.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: contraindication
candidates.comment: A medical restriction relation for a medical device or therapy, indicating a contraindication. Also called "medical warning", "precaution", "not recommended for". Examples: "Drug therapy contraindication 'Pregnancy'", "Medical device contraindication 'Pacemaker users'".

candidates.label: increasesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk amplification relation between a medical risk factor and the medical entity (condition, complication) whose likelihood it increases. Also called heightens risk of, raises risk of, predisposes to, contributes to risk of. Examples: Smoking increasesRiskOf lung cancer. High blood pressure increasesRiskOf heart attack. Obesity increasesRiskOf type 2 diabetes.

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".

chosen_property.label: includes
chosen_property.definition: To contain or comprise something as a part or component
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation phrase and instances.

candidates.label: includesObject
candidates.comment: A composition relation between an offer or product collection and the specific products and their quantities it contains. Also called composed of, contains, comprises, consists of, has as object. Examples: An offer includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 2 apples. A product collection includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 5 books. A demand includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 1 car.

candidates.label: includesAttraction
candidates.comment: An attraction inclusion relation between a tourist destination and a tourist attraction located within it. Also called contains attraction, destination attraction, features attraction. Examples: "A tourist destination includes an attraction like a museum.", "The city includes an attraction for historical sites.", "This destination features a famous includes attraction."

candidates.label: includedInHealthInsurancePlan
candidates.comment: A health insurance plan inclusion relation between a drug and a health insurance plan that covers it. Also called covered by plan, plan coverage, drug coverage. Examples: "A drug is included in a health insurance plan.", "The medication is covered by an included in health insurance plan.", "This drug is part of a specific health insurance plan."

candidates.label: includedInDataCatalog
candidates.comment: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included in data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included in data catalog."

candidates.label: includedDataCatalog
candidates.comment: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included data catalog."

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: includedComposition
candidates.comment: A composition inclusion relation between a music composition and a smaller music composition that is part of it. Also called part of composition, contains composition, movement of. Examples: "A symphony has an included composition as a movement.", "A musical work includes a composition.", "This composition contains several included compositions.". Distinct from hasPart, which is a general part-whole relation for creative works.

candidates.label: includesHealthPlanNetwork
candidates.comment: A health plan network inclusion relation between a health insurance plan and a network it covers. Also called plan network, covered network, network of plan. Examples: "A health insurance plan includes a health plan network.", "The plan covers an includes health plan network.", "This insurance plan features a specific network."

candidates.label: includesHealthPlanFormulary
candidates.comment: A health plan formulary inclusion relation between a health insurance plan and a formulary it covers. Also called plan formulary, covered formulary, formulary of plan. Examples: "A health insurance plan includes a health plan formulary.", "The plan covers an includes health plan formulary.", "This insurance plan features a specific formulary."

candidates.label: includedRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A risk factor inclusion relation between a medical risk estimator and a risk factor used in its calculation. Also called risk factor in calculation, factor considered, included element. Examples: "A medical risk estimator includes a risk factor of age.", "The estimator considers an included risk factor of smoking.", "This tool uses an included risk factor for calculation."
